concepts.title: Entering the Real World: Tasks of Adulthood

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Entering the Real World: Tasks of Adulthood' refers to.
questions.a: Adulthood opens into what the chapter calls the real world: higher education and work, intimate partnership and marriage, and eventually parenthood. Each step brings new roles, responsibilities and the need to balance personal goals with obligations to others.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Entering the Real World: Tasks of Adulthood'.
questions.a: Adulthood is the balancing act -- career, partnership and parenthood each demanding a share of the self.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Entering the Real World: Tasks of Adulthood' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: unit (source: kehe203.txt unit opener (unit iv adulthood, real world of higher education work marriage, roles and responsibilities))

concepts.title: Work, Marriage and Family: Institutions of Adult Life

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Work, Marriage and Family: Institutions of Adult Life' refers to.
questions.a: Adult life organises itself around institutions: the workplace, which structures income, identity and time; marriage, a social and legal partnership carrying mutual duties; and the family, where parenthood raises the next generation. Adjustment, communication and shared responsibility keep these institutions working.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Work, Marriage and Family: Institutions of Adult Life'.
questions.a: Work pays the bills, marriage shares the load, family gives it meaning -- institutions joined by adjustment.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Work, Marriage and Family: Institutions of Adult Life' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: unit (source: kehe203.txt unit opener and institution sections (work, marriage and family, adjustment, communication, shared responsibility))

concepts.title: Challenges and Coping in Adult Life

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Challenges and Coping in Adult Life' refers to.
questions.a: Adulthood carries predictable stresses -- career pressure, financial strain, family conflicts, and later, ageing parents and health changes. Coping rests on planning, health maintenance, social support and flexibility of roles as life's stages turn.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Challenges and Coping in Adult Life'.
questions.a: Stress is scheduled into adult life -- planning, health and support are the shock absorbers.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Challenges and Coping in Adult Life' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: unit (source: kehe203.txt unit opener and challenge sections (career and financial pressures, ageing, health, coping strategies, social support))
